messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: High error rate on decode/streaming pool us-west-2-decode-2. 15% request error, 40% increase in CUDA OOMs in the last 2m. Alert ID: INC-2180009876
maya: paging @oncall (oncall-bot)
aj: oncall here, looking now. what's the customer impact?
tom: seeing lots of `CUDA out of memory` in the logs. sample: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 3.54 GiB (GPU 0; 14.73 GiB total capacity)`
kevin: metrics: token churn spiked, median tokens/request jumped from ~120 to ~12k in last 10m. suspicious.
sara: we have a canary from partner-x that rolled out a prompt change ~11:10 that removed an explicit max_tokens cap. could be runaway generation.
emily: confirming: partner-x traffic routed to us-west-2-decode-2. their recent PR removed `max_tokens=256` from streaming call.
aj: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle partner-x at edge 2) enable global per-request token cap until patch 3) drain affected nodes from pool. doing 1 now.
maya: @aj please post throttling command you run and confirm rate limit id.
aj: ran `rwctl quota update --token cap --id=global-streaming --max-tokens=1024` — applied. also added rate-limit 10rps to partner-x prefix.
kevin: node-level: one pod shows repeated OOMs and CUDA errors causing container crashloops. I'll mark it as unschedulable and drain: `kubectl cordon decode-node-43 && kubectl drain decode-node-43 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
tom: logs from container: `Traceback (most recent call last): ... RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory during decoder forward` then `SIGABRT` and kube restart.
emily: rolling restart of decode pool to evict sticky KV cache instances. starting canary restart of 3 pods.
sara: customer-success-bot: partner-x reported several 502 drops and slow streaming for ~9 minutes, they filed a ticket. flagged P2.
maya: questions for postmortem: why didn't global safeguards prevent runaway token allocations? do we have per-request hard caps enforced at the runtime?
aj: current design: client libraries set `max_tokens` but runtime has soft guidance. we have token accounting but not a strict hard absolute limit per request. that gap is causing this.
kevin: adding mitigation patch to runtime: reject new streaming requests that request tokens > 4096 at the proxy level + enforce a hard token allocator cap. creating PR now.
tom: alternative short-term: enable decode node eviction of largest KV caches when GPU mem < 1GiB free. can patch config.
emily: deployed edge throttles and token cap; error rate dropped from 15% -> 3% in 5m. streaming error count down 80%.
aj: customer impact: partner-x 502s ~420 requests failed, other customers on same pool ~1500 requests slowed but not dropped. no data loss. We likely missed SLO for latency for ~13m window.
maya: notifying ops-brief and sending incident notification to partner-x CS. I'll draft status: initial mitigation applied, working on runtime hard cap and runtime patch targeted in next 2 hours, full postmortem TBD.
sara: oncall-bot: handoff to night oncall @kevin in 30m. kevin, please watch for residual OOMs and validate patched hard cap in staging then prod roll.
kevin: ack. reproductions: will run a synthetic with missing max_tokens to validate runtime reject. posting test script:```bash
# synthetic runaway test
python -c "import requests; payload={'prompt':'x'*10,'stream':True}; r=requests.post('$EDGE/stream',json=payload,timeout=180)"```
emily: note: we should add monitoring alert for token-rate-per-request > 2k to trigger before OOM cascade. filing alert.
maya: temporary customer comms sent. escalation: none requested. moving to incident review channel after stabilization. Thanks everyone. :heartpulse:
kevin: final check: disk and GPU metrics stable, no more crashloops. leaving node cordoned until patch. will run gradual uncordon after verifying stability.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2180009876 set to status: mitigated -> monitoring.
customer-success-bot: partner-x updated: we applied temporary throttles and token caps; engineering is deploying a runtime hard-limit patch; root cause likely a client-side config change that removed `max_tokens`. CS will follow up with their engineering team.
maya: postmortem owners: aj (mitigation), kevin (runtime patch), emily (deploy + monitoring), sara (customer comms). I'll schedule a blameless postmortem for tomorrow.
